# ViteHub

> Portable Agents for Vite, built on Server Primitives.

Rules for coding agents:

- Read the installed package exports and types before you write imports or options. When the installed packages, these docs, and remembered syntax disagree, follow the installed packages.
- Prefer the `vite-hub` distribution: register `vitehub()` from `vite-hub` in the Vite config and import Runtime Helpers from feature subpaths such as `vite-hub/kv`. Some pages use owner packages such as `@vite-hub/kv`; follow the style that the project already uses.
- Keep provider and host selection in the Vite config. Application code calls the same Runtime Helper on every host.
- Give an Agent authority only through Capabilities, Workspaces, Sources, or Channels. Do not pass application secrets or broad access to an Agent implicitly.
- Open the raw page for one feature, such as `https://vitehub.dev/raw/docs/kv.md`, before you write code. Raw pages contain agent-only details that the rendered site does not show. Do not load llms-full.txt for one task.
- Prove the change: run the Runtime Helper, Agent Invocation, webhook, or schedule, and inspect the generated `.vitehub/` state or provider output.
- Install the ViteHub skill for routed guidance: `npx skills add https://vitehub.dev --skill vitehub`.

## Overview

- [ViteHub](https://vitehub.dev/raw/index.md)

## Documentation Sets

- [ViteHub](https://vitehub.dev/llms-full.txt): Portable Agents for Vite, built on Server Primitives.

## When to use ViteHub

Use ViteHub when a Vite application needs portable server storage, queues, workflows, schedules, sandboxes, or other Server Primitives; when it needs inspectable Agent Definitions with explicit Capabilities and Workspaces; or when the same runtime behavior must deploy across supported hosts without leaking provider APIs into application code.

- [Choose a ViteHub layer](https://vitehub.dev/raw/docs/getting-started.md): Decide whether the job needs a Server Primitive, an Agent, or both.
- [Install ViteHub](https://vitehub.dev/raw/docs/getting-started/installation.md): Install the framework distribution or a focused owner package.
- [Compare ViteHub](https://vitehub.dev/raw/docs/compare.md): Compare ViteHub with NuxtHub, Mastra, and the Cloudflare Agents SDK, and see when ViteHub is the wrong choice.
- [Agent harness](https://vitehub.dev/raw/docs/agents/harness.md): See how ViteHub runs Codex, Claude Code, or a model loop with Capabilities, Workspaces, Sandboxes, and approvals.
